Countries around the world are turning to the highly polluting source of power in a bid to avoid shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. According to the International Energy Agency, global coal demand is forecast to rise by ​1.2% this year to a record 8.94 billion ‌tonnes. FRANCE 24’s Environment Editor Valerie Dekimpe has the details in this edition.

stories.title: Wild dogs record 2,500-mile trek across Zambia in search of a mate
stories.description: Scientists say the record-breaking journey by three brothers offers hope wildlife can survive growing pressures.

stories.title: Paige Bueckers’ $160,000 Minnesota impact: How did her $50,000 gift grow?
stories.description: Basketball sensation Paige Bueckers made headlines with her incredible donation of fifty thousand dollars to support families in Hopkins. This selfless act addressed crucial needs such as food and rent, igniting a wave of community spirit that resulted in an additional fifty thousand dollars raised. Bueckers’ efforts also brought attention to the valuable work of the ICA Food Shelf, emphasizing her strong ties to her hometown's welfare.

stories.title: Saudi football body vows action against Jota chants
stories.description: Cristiano Ronaldo called for life bans after rival fans taunted Al-Hilal's Ruben Neves over the death of his friend and former Portugal teammate Diogo Jota.

stories.title: Taiping eatery owner fined RM18,000 over halal cert offence
stories.description: He had displayed decorations bearing the words ‘Allah’ and ‘Muhammad’ in his restaurant.

stories.title: The producer of Fleabag and Baby Reindeer's tip for finding a hit? Don't look for one
stories.description: Theatre producer Francesca Moody has a remarkable record of spotting shows that go on to have wide success. At the Edinburgh Fringe festival, she told NPR about what she looks for in a performance.

stories.title: Keziah Jones goes symphonic
stories.description: This week arts24 talks to Nigerian Blues Funk Artist Keziah Jones ahead of his Symphonic premier at la Scène Musicale on September 29 as part of Jazz & Musique du Monde season. He tells FRANCE 24's Marjorie Hache about his music and about working with arranger Pierre Bertrand. Plus, we take a look at new releases by Beck, Miley Cyrus and Beabadobee.

stories.title: Germany news: Merz urges CDU discipline as pressure grows
stories.description: Chancellor Friedrich Merz has urged his party to stay disciplined as pressure grows over his leadership. Meanwhile, Germany's homeownership rate has fallen to its lowest level in 20 years. DW has the latest.

stories.title: YPM FC juara sulung Liga Rakyat Pahang 1st Piala Al-Sultan Abdullah
stories.description: YPM FC menewaskan Majlis Daerah Raub 2-1 pada aksi final di Stadium Darul Makmur untuk membawa pulang hadiah wang tunai RM40,000.

stories.title: Sam Altman and Dario Amodei, China does not agree with your AI plea
stories.description: China firmly dismisses pleas from prominent American tech executives to curb advancements in artificial intelligence, labelling such warnings as mere fearmongering. Encouraging international collaboration, Chinese authorities stress the importance of keeping AI development accessible and advantageous for everyone. State-run media assert that American leaders are leveraging safety issues to obstruct China's development, despite local officials recognizing potential dangers posed by automated technologies.

stories.title: How will EU respond to Russian attack on train near Polish border?
stories.description: The EU's top diplomat said Monday that Russian strikes which hit a Warsaw-bound train near Ukraine's border with Poland shortly after top Western figures passed through were meant to "scare" off Kyiv's backers. "It is clearly meant to scare Western countries from supporting Ukraine, from going to Ukraine to show support," foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said, urging Kyiv's backers to do "the opposite". France 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels.

stories.title: Eurocrat salaries, staff numbers face cuts in next long-term budget
stories.description: The Irish presidency wrote that a majority of countries support slashing cuts to save money.

stories.title: Tangguh permohonan pengampunan Najib budi bicara Agong, kata PM
stories.description: Anwar Ibrahim berkata peranannya adalah memberi pandangan berdasarkan undang-undang dan nasihat peguam negara.

stories.title: 'What makes China work despite the pain in society?' asks analyst Dan Wang
stories.description: In this edition of Perspective, FRANCE 24’s Stuart Norval speaks to Dan Wang, a China expert whose book ‘Breakneck: China’s Quest to Engineer the Future’ is a New York Times bestseller. It takes a close look at Chinese life and draws from Wang’s own ten years of living there. Wang says the China and the US are some of the most similar people in the world, as they are both hustlers and take shortcuts.

stories.title: ‘Sekadar pandangan Umno’, Anwar ulas cabaran PRU awal
stories.description: Perdana menteri berkata, keutamaannya adalah memastikan kerajaan kekal stabil demi negara.

stories.title: Decision to defer Najib’s pardon bid is Agong’s prerogative, says PM
stories.description: Anwar Ibrahim says his role was to give his views based on the law and the attorney-general's advice.

stories.title: Europe hesitates as Russian attacks escalate

stories.title: Guru didakwa pukul murid kini ditempatkan di PPD
stories.description: JPN P Pinang berkata, tindakan diambil sejurus dapat aduan waris agar siasatan dapat dijalankan secara teratur.

stories.title: French 2027 presidential elections: Why Gen Z has mobilised for Mélenchon
stories.description: 🇫🇷 French far-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc #Mélenchon is both highly controversial and a #GenZ favourite. Mélenchon's young supporters express admiration for his promises to stage a "citizen's revolution", redistrubute wealth, fight #climatechange and support #Palestine. The candidate's critics have accused him of complancency towards #Russia and antisemitism. Despite being divisive, recent polls predict that Mélenchon will qualify for the second round of #France's 2027 presidential #election, where he would likely face far-right candidate Marine #LePen. So, why has France's Gen Z mobilised for Mélenchon? 🔴 FRANCE 24's Gabrielle Nadler spoke to young voters to find out.

stories.title: Should the brakes be put on AI?
stories.description: US President Donald Trump says he is worried about America giving China an edge in the Artificial Intelligence market if too many rules and regulations are put on it. In recent days industry insiders, including top executives at Open AI and Anthropic, have once again sounded the alarm, saying that the way AI is being developed could threaten humanity and calling for more checks to be put in place.

stories.title: The London hospital funded by donors who invested in the slave trade
stories.description: St Barts is one of many UK institutions whose benefactors were involved in the trafficking of enslaved Africans Inside the Great Hall of St Bartholomew’s North Wing, alongside stately portraits of the apostle from whom London’s oldest hospital takes its name and King Henry VIII, extravagant commemorative boards adorn the walls. The Great Hall was a grand, formal space where governors weighed their philanthropic donations and drafted their wills, many while investing in the stock of companies built on the trafficking of enslaved Africans. Today, many of those donors are commemorated in acrylic gold paint on the boards. Continue reading...

stories.title: Star Japanese novelist jumps from killer thrillers to children’s books
stories.description: Asako Yuzuki, famous for thrillers like Butter, pivots to children's literature with her new book, "Mari the Unwonderful Witch."

stories.title: Trump criticises 'negative forces' seeking to slow AI development
stories.description: US President Donald Trump on Sunday slammed critics of artificial intelligence (AI) who warned firms to slow down development, branding them "negative" forces. The comments came soon after OpenAI CEO Sam Altman announced his company will not go public this year, citing safety concerns.

stories.title: Ukraine: AfD questions German aid, Berlin remains committed
stories.description: Emboldened by its win in Saxony-Anhalt, the far-right Alternative for Germany wants the government to change its Ukraine and Russia policies. Berlin is staying the course, but support is fading — especially in the east.

stories.title: Climate catastrophe leaves Nepal mourning while the search for the missing continues
stories.description: The himalayan flash flood that devastated northern Nepal on August 26 was an unprecedented disaster. The death toll continues to rise, with nearly 1,400 people now confirmed dead and 5,130 still missing, including around 600 foreign nationals from 35 countries.

stories.title: The Crusades: How a medieval Holy War still shapes politics
stories.description: In 1095, the Catholic Church launched the Crusades: wars that left millions dead and whose legacy still shapes political and ideological conflicts.

stories.title: Joyce dismisses threats of 'tanked economy' from negative migration rates
stories.description: One Nation's treasury spokesperson Barnaby Joyce says his party is prepared to put the will of the people ahead of the opinions of economists, as he faces claims on ABC's National Forum that net negative migration would "tank" Australia's economy.

stories.title: Africa’s richest man aiming to make $23bn from continent’s biggest-ever IPO
stories.description: Public offering of Aliko Dangote’s Nigerian oil refinery business could swell his net wealth by two-thirds The fortune of Africa’s richest person could swell by two thirds to nearly $60bn (£44bn) after his refinery in Nigeria listed publicly in the continent’s biggest-ever initial public offering. If Monday’s flotation of Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals on the Nigerian exchange goes to plan, then Aliko Dangote will add a further $23bn (£17bn) to his $35bn net worth. Continue reading...

stories.title: Von der Leyen to skip Carney speech in EU Parliament

stories.title: Travis Kelce’s $5.35m Ohio home sparks neighbor concerns

Bratenahl Mayor Keith Benjamin addressed the issue, stressing that the village welcomes high-profile residents while respecting their privacy. The property, near Kelce’s childhood home, spans 3.5 acres and features eight bedrooms, 11 bathrooms, a theater, fitness center, sauna, guest cottage and a former speakeasy.

stories.title: European firms unprepared for China shock as EU tries to cut reliance on Beijing

stories.title: EU leaders urge unity after Russian strike on train
stories.description: Russia's drone attack on a train near the Ukraine-Poland border has triggered EU calls to up support for Kyiv. Allies of Ukraine should show they "are not scared," said the bloc's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas.

stories.title: BioNTech lung cancer drug extends survival versus chemotherapy

stories.description: The EU's top diplomat said Monday that Russian strikes which hit a Warsaw-bound train near Ukraine's border with Poland shortly after top Western figures passed through were meant to "scare" off Kyiv's backers. France 24's correspondent in Kyiv, Gulliver Cragg, has the latest.

stories.description: Asaduddin Owaisi's AIMIM is actively pursuing alliances with opposition parties in preparation for the upcoming elections in Uttar Pradesh. AIMIM's strategy revolves around consolidating its Muslim voter base to compete with major parties like the Samajwadi Party and Congress, which are also targeting this demographic. Should the opposition remain divided, the BJP could exploit these fractures for electoral gains.

stories.title: Munir fails Mecca test: Why Pak's field marshal is not riding to rescue MBS
Thousands demand end to violence in Mexican cartel hotspot

stories.title: Thousands rally in support of Brazil's Lula as election campaigning heats up
stories.description: With Brazil set to hold a Presidential election on October 4th, supporters of both incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula Da Silva and his main opponent Flavio Bolsonaro have been taking to the streets. Polls have the candidates, who are on opposite ends of political spectrum, neck and neck.

stories.title: Dozens arrested as Turkish police raid LGBTQ bars, activists' homes
stories.description: Turkish police on Sunday made dozens of arrests in a slew of raids on gay bars and the homes of LGBTQ activists. Authorities said the raids came in the context of the "Decade of the Family" proclaimed by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, aimed at "protecting our children, the institution of the family and social order".

stories.title: A 'complicated autumn' awaits Sweden after knife-edge vote
stories.description: Sweden's general election remained too close to call early Monday, with nearly 90 percent of votes counted. Four opposition parties led by Social Democrat Magdalena Andersson held a one-seat parliamentary lead over Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson's right-wing bloc, which includes the Sweden Democrats, as both leaders said they were ready to govern.

stories.title: Takaichi seeks closer cooperation with IEA on energy security

stories.title: The powerful millionaires hiding in plain sight
stories.description: They own car dealerships, law firms, dental practices, and restaurant chains. Collectively, these overlooked business owners hold far more wealth than the Forbes 400 — and wield considerable political power.

stories.title: ‘They drove us from our land’: Thousands displaced by Yemen conflict
stories.description: According to the UN, more than 86,000 people have been displaced in Yemen since July, following fighting between the Iran-backed Houthis rebels and government forces. Many have fled to refugee camps in government-controlled Aden, while others have headed to neighbouring Djibouti.

stories.title: Minister flies to Pilbara after report of up to 15 kids living unsupervised

stories.description: Israel's culture minister wants to strip the makers of a documentary on Israel's Gaza offensive of their citizenship. He accused the two of seeking "applause from antisemites around the world."

stories.title: Fundraiser launched for children of woman who died in Nelson

stories.title: The 'kooky' show that lured Celeste Barber back to the theatre

The man, 57, and his two children, seven and four, who are also Indonesian citizens, were discovered deceased in a bungalow in Kuta on Sunday morning. Continue reading...
